51/G.goal: Explain how to convert a minimum-time all-POI VR tour into a time-weighted travelling-salesman problem and recover a valid path that limits exposure duration to reduce cybersickness.
51/G.achieves: It gives the learner an optimization approach for VR navigation that can be used to analyze or design virtual tour experiences in the course's XR system-development and optimization work.

51/O1.goal: Describe how cybersickness-related exposure-duration limits in semi-interactive VR tours lead to POI path-optimization problems.
51/O1.achieves: It gives the learner the user-experience criterion needed to evaluate and constrain VR navigation design in the course's optimization topics.

51/O2.goal: Model the minimum-time all-POI VR tour as a weighted graph whose edge weights are travel times estimated by the natural walking-speed model.
51/O2.achieves: It gives the learner a quantitative navigation model that can be used to compare and optimize virtual tour routes in the course's XR development case study.

51/O3.goal: Transform the minimum-time POI tour into a complete time-weighted travelling-salesman problem and describe how to recover a valid original-graph path while respecting a cybersickness time threshold.
51/O3.achieves: It lets the learner apply a standard graph-optimization method to generate VR navigation paths that reduce exposure time, supporting the course's aim of implementing XR systems with optimization-aware design.
